timelines.title: One parish, three church homes
timelines.intro: The institution founded as St. George in Detroit continues today as Divine Providence in Southfield. Its church buildings changed; the parish community endured.

events.title: St. George parish founded in Detroit
events.detail: Detroit's Lithuanian Catholics established the parish whose institutional life continues as Divine Providence.

events.title: Two Detroit church homes lost
events.detail: Two successive parish church sites were taken for highway construction. The community rebuilt after each loss.

events.title: Lithuanian national-parish status secured
events.detail: The parish requested non-territorial Lithuanian status; the Archdiocese of Detroit accepted it in writing on December 31, 1968.

events.title: Present Southfield church consecrated
events.detail: Parishioners funded and built the church, rectory, and cultural center that remain the community's home today.

events.title: Living parish under restructuring review
events.detail: Lithuanian worship continues, while the parish's future is being considered in the Archdiocese of Detroit restructuring. No closure decree has been issued.

sources.title: In Writing: The 1968 Letter That Made Divine Providence a National Parish
sources.citation: Reproduces the December 31, 1968 Archdiocese of Detroit letter and cites Dievo Apvaizdos Parapija 1908–1973, pp. 48–51.

sources.title: Southfield's Divine Providence Lithuanian church seeks to remain a standalone ethnic parish
sources.citation: Michigan Catholic Tribune · current-status reporting checked July 27, 2026.
